categories.reading: Case-mix-adjusted commercial hospital prices averaged 253 percent of simulated Medicare prices, with wide state and provider variation.
categories.why_not_expected_value: Medicare is an administratively set reference and may not equal an adequate competitive payment for every hospital, service, or market.

categories.reading: CBO finds commercial hospital and physician prices higher and more variable than Medicare prices; provider market power and consolidation consistently raise commercial prices.
categories.why_not_expected_value: No current national same-service physician ratio with an attached access, input-cost, and quality floor is locked in this artifact.

categories.reading: US retail pharmaceutical spending per person was the OECD's highest and more than twice its average.
categories.why_not_expected_value: Spending combines net prices, prescribing, therapeutic mix, quantities, margins, tax treatment, and retail-versus-hospital dispensing; it is not a drug-price index.

next_gate: For hospitals and physicians, construct same-service commercial price distributions with Medicare adequacy and access floors. For drugs, separate net price, therapeutic mix, quantity, and retail-versus-hospital scope before scoring.
